content.title: Changing the time range clears a locked allocation selection
content.intent: Prove a supported time-range change clears an existing locked allocation selection so the card does not keep stale focus after context changes.
content.technique_notes: Applied state_flow because the promise is a context-change reset after a maintained selection. Depends on the lock/unlock path because a locked segment is the required precondition. No separate time-range value partition was minted because the source states only a generic time-range context change, not the supported range set. Budget ceiling=8 existed; budget_cut kept this scenario with the highest score due to stale-context risk.

content.title: Lock and unlock an allocation segment by clicking it
content.intent: Prove clicking a segment maintains a focused allocation state and clicking the same segment again clears that lock.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning across allocation segments because the click-lock behavior should be uniform for every slice. covering_array on asset_class degraded to effective_t=1 from requested strength 2 because only one input existed, so this scenario sweeps Equities, Fixed Income, Alternatives, Cash, and Commodities as equivalent representatives. Budget ceiling=8 existed; budget_cut kept this scenario as a core interaction path.

content.title: Hover an allocation segment to focus the matching legend item
content.intent: Prove hovering any allocation segment provides transient focus feedback by expanding the segment and highlighting the matching legend item.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning across allocation segments because the hover affordance is stated once and should behave consistently for every slice. covering_array on asset_class degraded to effective_t=1 from requested strength 2 because only one input existed, so this scenario sweeps Equities, Fixed Income, Alternatives, Cash, and Commodities as equivalent representatives. I did not split a separate center-content scenario because **gap-3** already records that the selected-allocation replacement content is underspecified. Budget ceiling=8 existed; budget_cut kept this scenario as a primary discovery path.

content.title: Review the default portfolio allocation breakdown
content.intent: Prove the allocation card renders the default donut data, center total, and legend fields needed to compare asset classes before any interaction.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to treat the five source-defined asset classes as the full default rendered set rather than separate outcome-changing paths. No boundary, negative, auth, or a11y expansion applied because the source specifies fixed read-only display content and no input, gate, or alternate empty/error state. Budget ceiling=8 existed; budget_cut kept this scenario because all later interaction checks rely on the correct default render.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] Applied eqp to default, hover, and click interactions because each promise should hold uniformly across the five allocation slices. Applied state_flow to the time-range reset because it depends on a prior locked state and a subsequent context transition.

[applicability] Did not apply bva, negative, overflow_underflow, pagination, auth, crud, idempotency, concurrency, file_media, notification, perf, responsiveness, mobile-native, web-form, rest-graphql-api, search-list, or stateful-flow profiles because the source describes a fixed read-only dashboard card with no constrained user input, persistence, role gate, collection pagination, external side effect, or alternate supported surface-specific contract.
[value_score] Ranked highest because stale locked focus after a time-range change would present incorrect analytical context and directly undermine decision-making.
[value_score] Ranked second because locking and unlocking determines whether the feature supports sustained comparison beyond transient hover.
[value_score] Ranked third because hover is the primary in-chart affordance for focusing a slice and revealing the linked legend state.
[value_score] Ranked fourth because correct default content is foundational, but the interaction failures above would mislead the user more severely once the card is visible.
